vice.

Be specific by describing what the nominee did, not just their qualities.

Focus on the impact of their actions.

Make clear what the specific achievements are.

Avoid jargon and technical terms.

Include facts and figures wherever possible.

Demonstrate sustained impact by including examples from different periods or projects to show ongoing commitment. If one event is highlighted, make clear why it was exceptional and how it reflects the nominee’s wider contribution.

What to avoid

Do not just list the nominee’s career history or achievements.

Do not focus on long service as this is not a long service award.

Do not use vague statements or generic praise (for example, “they are well respected”) without giving clear examples.

Do not submit nominations that simply describe someone doing their job well - focus on what is truly exceptional.

Example of a good nomination

This nomination is good because it:

focuses on the nominee’s personal actions and impact

explains the context clearly

emphasises the significance of the contributions

does not just list roles or rely solely on the length of service

What issues did the nominee face in their role?

Chief Officer Anita Patel served on a cargo vessel, leading a small crew through a particularly demanding shipping season. Her role required her to oversee daily operations, ensure the safety and wellbeing of all crew members, and manage complex logistics, often with limited resources and under tight deadlines.

The ship regularly faced unpredictable weather and long periods at sea, which placed additional pressure on both the team and Chief Officer Patel. Despite these challenges, she was quick to notice that many seafarers struggled with feelings of isolation and uncertainty about where to seek help.

When she later transitioned to a shore-based role, she recognised that these issues were widespread and not limited to her own vessel. Motivated by what she had observed, she took on the responsibility of creating a new support programme for seafarers, starting from zero, with no existing framework or resources to build upon.

What did the nominee do?

After recognising the difficulties faced by crew members, she made a point of listening to their concerns and understanding the issues that affected their wellbeing. Rather than simply carrying out her usual duties, she took the initiative to design a support programme that addressed the real needs of seafarers. She spent her own time developing resources and running drop-in sessions, making sure that help was available to anyone who needed it.

She also created easy-to-read guides for new joiners, ensuring that even those unfamiliar with the organisation could access support. She worked closely with other departments to make the programme available across different ships, showing a commitment to improving the lives of seafarers beyond her immediate team.

Furthermore, she shared their approach with other companies, allowing the benefits of the programme to reach even more people in the maritime sector. Her actions were not part of her formal responsibilities but stemmed from a desire to make a lasting difference for others.

What was the result / impact of the nominee’s action?

As a result of her efforts, seafarers felt more supported and confident, both at sea and ashore. In the first year, over 50 crew members used the new support programme, and feedback showed that people felt less isolated and more able to ask for help. The scheme was adopted by two other companies, extending its positive impact beyond her own organisation. Reports of wellbeing concerns dropped by 40%, and the programme became a model for supporting seafarers across the sector. These outstanding results and effort, make Chief Officer Patel deserving of the Merchant Navy Medal for Meritorious Service.

Because of these actions, new recruits reported that they felt more supported and confident. Three other ships adopted the mentoring scheme. Reports of workplace concerns dropped by 50%, and more women and LGBT+ seafarers joined the company.

After the delivery of the new joiners brief and workshops, reported bullying cases fell by a third across two vessels. Two partner companies adopted the toolkit the nominee developed. New joiner surveys showed higher confidence about reporting concerns.

Example of a poorly written nomination

This nomination is poor because it does not explain what the nominee personally did or why it was exceptional. It’s just a list of job history and general praise.

What issues did the nominee face in their role?

Captain Johnson has worked as a Chief Officer for several years, responsible for overseeing cargo operations, maintaining safety standards and ensuring compliance with company procedures. His duties include supervising crew, managing paperwork, and coordinating with port authorities. He is known for being reliable, and getting the job done. He is hardworking and respected by everyone.

What did the nominee do?

With more than 30 years of experience at sea, Captain Johnson has steadily progressed to a senior position through tireless dedication and always going the extra mile. Throughout his 40-year career, he has obtained numerous qualifications (a full list is provided below) and held a variety of important roles, including Chief Officer and Master on several vessels (a full list of his positions is provided below). His impressive record includes extensive service on different ship types and a long list of professional achievements. As demonstrated by the positions held and his long career, Captain Johnson is very committed to his work, and he enjoys the respect from colleagues at all levels.
